\textbf{Taken on trust: Landau's formula.} For fixed $x>1$,
\[\sum_{0<\Im\rho\le T}x^{\rho}=-\frac{T}{2\pi}\Lambda(x)+\order(\log T),\]
where the sum runs over all nontrivial zeros $\rho$ of zeta with imaginary part in $(0,T]$. In this form it is a theorem, and it does \emph{not} assume that the zeros lie on the critical line. Now suppose every zero up to height $T$ has the form $\rho_n=\frac12+it_n$. This is verified numerically for all zeros used in this book; that it holds at every height is the Riemann hypothesis, which is open. Then $x^{\rho_n}=x^{1/2}e^{it_n\log x}$ (Chapter~\ref{ch:complex}), and dividing by $\sqrt x$ gives \eqref{eq:fourier-transform-landau} plus an error $\order(\log T)/\sqrt x$.
